note: Verifies TLS expiry semantics (Part A, deterministic) and ACME ARI protocol behavior (Part B, real ACME against a local pebble CA). No statistical distribution applies: Part A is a pass/fail handshake observation with a fixed OpenSSL verify code; Part B is a protocol walk whose returned window/lifetime are CA-policy values, reported as observed on 2026-06-23.

part_a_expiry_semantics.environment: OpenSSL 3.5.6, local EC P-256 root CA, short-lived leaf (20s), Python ssl client with CERT_REQUIRED + hostname check

observations.claim: While the short-lived cert is still within NotAfter, a verifying client completes the TLS handshake.
The instant NotAfter passes with renewal stalled, the same client breaks AT the TLS handshake — no grace period, application code never runs.

part_b_acme_ari.environment: pebble (ghcr.io/letsencrypt/pebble:latest, PEBBLE_VA_ALWAYS_VALID=1), hand-written pure-Python ACME client (ES256 JWS)

observations.claim: Ordering under the 'shortlived' profile yields a lifetime the CA chose, not the client.
observations.value: NotBefore 2026-06-23T10:06:25Z, NotAfter 2026-06-29T10:06:24Z, lifetime 144h (pebble default, not LE policy)

observations.claim: The CA's renewalInfo (ARI) endpoint returns a suggested renewal TIME WINDOW plus a Retry-After, not a single instant.
The ARI path segment (CertID) is derived from the certificate itself (AKI keyIdentifier + serial), so each cert has a unique ARI URL.
observations.evidence: partB/acme_ari.py computes b64url(AKI) + '.' + b64url(serial DER octets)

observations.claim: pebble still exposes the ARI endpoint under the draft path name; the client must read renewalInfo from the directory rather than hardcoding it.
observations.value: path carries 'draft-ietf-acme-ari-03'; the standard itself is finalized as RFC 9773 (cited)

cited_not_measured.claim: Public TLS cert max lifetime shrinks from 2026-03, reaching 47 days by 2029 (398d -> 200d -> 100d -> 47d).
cited_not_measured.source: CA/Browser Forum ballot SC-081 / Let's Encrypt announcements

cited_not_measured.claim: ARI is finalized as RFC 9773 (was draft-ietf-acme-ari).
Real Let's Encrypt short-lived profile lifetimes/windows differ from pebble's 144h default.
cited_not_measured.source: Let's Encrypt docs (pebble is a test CA, 'without actual enforcement')
post's client support table, from each client's changelog/docs

cited_not_measured.claim: Short lifetimes let mass-revocation be absorbed by expiry, reducing OCSP/CRL dependence.
cited_not_measured.source: ARI design rationale (reasoned, not measured here)

not_measured.real_ca_policy: Only pebble's default 144h + window were observed. Production CA numbers are cited.
not_measured.dcv_failures: Domain validation was auto-satisfied (PEBBLE_VA_ALWAYS_VALID=1). DCV failure is abstracted by Part A's stall case.
not_measured.pebble_version: pebble pulled as :latest, not pinned — exact numbers may drift on re-run; the mechanism does not.
